notes: **Work.** Work done by a constant force is the dot product W = F·s = Fs cosθ; it is maximum when force and displacement are parallel and zero when they are perpendicular.
**Torque.** The moment of a force about a point is τ = r × F, with magnitude rF sinθ and direction given by the right-hand rule; torque measures the turning effect.
**Angular momentum.** The angular momentum of a particle is L = r × p = r × mv, and for a rigid body rotating about a fixed axis L = Iω.
**Newton's law for rotation.** The net external torque equals the rate of change of angular momentum, τ = dL/dt, in exact analogy with F = dp/dt.
**Conservation.** If the net external torque on a system is zero, its angular momentum stays constant — a spinning skater speeds up when pulling in their arms.
